reason: The 2026-07-22 transcript has Lina saying reps must not unarchive, because they could reactivate customers who are now ineligible, and Kobi agreeing that only Ops can unarchive. The 07-28 demo repeats that archived records must be unlocked by the Ops team. WAGR-271 (Done) says 'Let Reps pull an archived Sign-Up back' and has no Ops-only restriction. No later meeting or Jira ticket reverses this or covers it. Confidence stays medium because no one has checked whether the built button is visible to Reps.
q1: Found, all words verbatim. Doc 1BRZjXeg... (title 'Wagertech <> Jumpr: Weekly Sync - 2026/07/22 11:30 EDT - Notes by Gemini'), fetched lines 1013-1014: 'Lina Ceniccola: if it's like if it's part of the I just want to make sure that once they archive it they can't unarchchive' and 'Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, like we can restrict that. So only like ops can unarchive something.' Caveat: the claim joins lines out of order. The third segment ('you can still go in and you can move the status to in progress') comes from the 00:56:15 block, about 2 minutes BEFORE the Lina/Kobi exchange, which is at 00:58:25, not 00:56:15. The Gemini summary (line 90) confirms the exchange: Lina wants to stop unauthorized users from unarchiving, and Kobi says access can be restricted to operations staff.
q2: Supports the claim. Context: at 00:56:15 Kobi demos that reps cannot edit archived sign-ups but ops can move them back to In Progress. At 00:57:14 Lina gives the jail/Horseshoe example: 'we don't really want the rep to control when they put that customer ... back active again cuz like they could be ineligible now.' At 00:58:25 she asks that they cannot unarchive, and Kobi answers 'only like ops can unarchive something.' This is an explicit client requirement with a stated business reason, and Jumpr accepted it. It is not a hypothetical, and no one walks it back later in the meeting. The talk that follows is only about the status model (archived stays a status, the button opens a reason box).
q3: No reversal. L1345 (2026-07-28, raw transcript 00:30:38) supports the Ops-only intent: 'archive status none of it is editable by rep. So this these records do need to be unlocked by the ops team', then the Reactivate button demo. Kobi was probably logged in as an admin or ops user ('logged in as ... admin under more ops'), so the demo does not show what a Rep sees. L1725 (08-13) and L1872 (08-17, auto-reactivate immediately) are about the system automation (WAGR-219). They do not give reps manual control. L2348 (09-02) restricts the Player/Referrer reactivate to Ops only, which shows the same pattern elsewhere. L3393 (09-30) is about Deals. None of these changes the Sign-Up rule.
q4: Not covered. Live WAGR-271: Done (resolved 2026-09-14), unassigned, 1 comment (2026-07-29, Asana import). The description's objective is 'Let Reps pull an archived Sign-Up back into the working queue.' The button is visible only when Status = Archived. Nothing restricts it by persona, and the comment only decides the target status (In Progress). JQL 'reactivate OR unarchive' returned 24 issues: WAGR-219 (auto-reactivate, Jumpr Review), WAGR-158 (Referrer Reactivate), Player and Deal items. None restricts the Sign-Up Reactivate to Ops. JQL 'archived AND (ops OR permission)' returned WAGR-494 (Sign-Up access cleanup, Open), which deals with rep direct-edit and delete access and tells the team to capture Ops-only Archive needs as persona requirements, but does not name the Reactivate button or flow. It also returned WAGR-351 (Done), which locks fraud-confirmed records only. WAGR-495 (access matrix, Open, 0 comments) does not list WAGR-271. At most WAGR-494/495 are a natural place to add the fix.
